- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict early spikes; correct by adding 0.1–0.3 to forecasted values for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overpredict early drops; correct by subtracting 0.1–0.3 from forecasted values for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., >0.8), model often overshoots in the immediate 1–3 days; apply a 10–20% downward correction to the first 3 forecasted days.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (15+ day) trends when sentiment is volatile; increase forecasted values by 0.1–0.2 per day for the final 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to overcorrect; apply a 0.05–0.1 smoothing factor to reduce volatility in forecasted values.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion; if sentiment is high for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.05–0.1 per day until sentiment stabilizes or drops.
